questions.stem:
Read the following passage and answer questions 1–10 based on it.

India's space programme, led by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), has __(1)__ itself as one of the most cost-effective space agencies in the world. Despite __(2)__ on a comparatively modest budget, ISRO has achieved __(3)__ milestones. The Mars Orbiter Mission, launched in 2013, made India the first Asian nation to __(4)__ Martian orbit on its __(5)__ attempt. In 2017, ISRO set a world record by __(6)__ 104 satellites in a single launch vehicle. These successes have greatly __(7)__ India's standing in the global space community. The Chandrayaan missions have __(8)__ valuable data about the Moon's surface, including evidence of water molecules. Looking ahead, ISRO __(9)__ to launch Gaganyaan, India's first manned spaceflight. Such ambitions clearly __(10)__ that India's journey among the stars has only just begun.

Blank (1): Choose the correct word.
questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Established itself as' = positioned or proven itself to be (in a field). ISRO has proven itself as cost-effective. Trap: 'lost itself as' is meaningless; 'destroyed' and 'removed' are negative, contradicting the positive context of the passage.

questions.stem:
(Passage repeated in exam setting — same passage as Q1.)

Blank (2): 'Despite __(2)__ on a comparatively modest budget'
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Operating on a budget' = working within financial limits. This is the standard collocation for organizations managing within financial constraints. Trap: 'investing' would imply placing money somewhere for returns (wrong context); 'spending lavishly' contradicts 'modest budget'; 'wasting' implies misuse of funds.

C is correct. The entire passage praises ISRO's achievements — 'remarkable milestones' (extraordinary, noteworthy) fits the tone. Trap: 'ordinary', 'minor', and 'forgettable' all downplay achievements, contradicting the passage's celebratory tone and specific examples (first Asian Mars mission, 104-satellite record).

questions.stem: Blank (4): '...the first Asian nation to __(4)__ Martian orbit on its...'
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Enter Martian orbit' = reach and begin orbiting Mars — the precise achievement of the Mars Orbiter Mission. Trap: 'miss Martian orbit' contradicts the success; 'leave' and 'escape' imply departing from orbit (not arriving at it). The mission entered orbit on its first attempt, which is the next blank's context.

questions.stem: Blank (5): '...first Asian nation to enter Martian orbit on its __(5)__ attempt.'
questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Maiden attempt' = the first attempt (often used for firsts: maiden voyage, maiden speech, maiden century). India succeeded on its FIRST try — a historic achievement. Trap: 'final attempt' would imply multiple tries before success; 'repeated' means more than once; 'failed' directly contradicts the success described.

questions.stem: Blank (6): 'ISRO set a world record by __(6)__ 104 satellites in a single launch vehicle.'
questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Launching satellites' = sending them into orbit using a rocket. ISRO's PSLV-C37 mission (2017) launched 104 satellites in one go — a world record at the time. Trap: 'losing', 'cancelling', and 'destroying' all imply failure or negative outcomes, contradicting the record-setting achievement.

questions.stem: Blank (7): 'These successes have greatly __(7)__ India's standing in the global space community.'
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Boosted India's standing' = improved and elevated India's reputation and position. The passage describes achievements, so their effect must be positive. Trap: 'damaged', 'reduced', and 'questioned' all imply a negative effect on reputation, directly contradicting the positive tone established by describing record-setting successes.

questions.stem: Blank (8): 'The Chandrayaan missions have __(8)__ valuable data about the Moon's surface...'
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Yielded valuable data' = produced or generated meaningful scientific data as a result of the missions. 'Yield' = produce as a result. Trap: 'ignored' and 'hidden' contradict obtaining data; 'wasted' contradicts 'valuable.' Note: 'collected' would also work conceptually, but 'yielded' is the more precise scientific term for missions that generate findings.

questions.stem: Blank (9): 'Looking ahead, ISRO __(9)__ to launch Gaganyaan, India's first manned spaceflight.'
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'ISRO aims to launch' = ISRO plans and intends to launch. 'Aim to + verb' expresses a goal or aspiration. Trap: 'refuses to launch' contradicts the stated ambition; 'fails to launch' would mean the mission didn't happen (contradicting future-tense ambition); 'hesitates' implies uncertainty, while the passage's tone is one of confident ambition.

questions.stem: Blank (10): 'Such ambitions clearly __(10)__ that India's journey among the stars has only just begun.'
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Clearly indicate that' = show clearly or make evident that. The ambitious plans signal (indicate) that India's space story is far from finished. Trap: 'deny' would mean the ambitions contradict the statement about an unfinished journey (illogical); 'mask' and 'obscure' mean to hide or conceal — the opposite of 'clearly' making something evident.
